title: True Sea Moss: trust comes before the *benefit stack*
dek: A one-page creative strategy specimen for Ivan Tsvilik. This is a strategic hold, not a recommendation to advertise through an unresolved proof gap.
lens: Functional food · trust repair · regulated claims
sources: True Sea Moss site + Whole Foods release + FDA recall record
footer_right: TRUE SEA MOSS · NOT CLIENT WORK

sections.heading: the message *gap*
sections.body:
The public homepage leads with scale proof, ocean sourcing, daily ritual, and a wide benefit stack. A January 2026 FDA-posted recall involving all flavors and sizes manufactured before January 9 is also easy for a skeptical buyer to find. The FDA now marks that recall completed and terminated, but the current homepage does not visibly explain the operational change.

That changes the creative job. Before another broad wellness ad, True Sea Moss needs current-batch proof that can survive the buyer's trust question. Concept A is blocked until the brand supplies that evidence. Concept B is a lower-claim taste-and-routine direction, but it should not be used to obscure the recall history.

rows.claim: The recall is a verified public trust event.
rows.evidence: The FDA record says Diva Fam recalled all flavors, sizes, and batch numbers of True Sea Moss gel manufactured before January 9, 2026 because of missing regulatory authorization and temperature-monitoring records. The FDA page says the recall has been completed and terminated; no illnesses were reported in the announcement.

rows.claim: The brand subsequently announced a Whole Foods expansion.
rows.evidence: An April 22 release says three sea moss gels entered select Whole Foods stores and emphasizes transparent production and consciously sourced ingredients.

rows.claim: The current homepage spreads attention across scale, sourcing, ritual, and many benefits.
rows.evidence: The site cites customer and subscriber numbers, wildcrafted sourcing, energy, focus, digestion, immune support, metabolism, skin, hair, and daily minerals.

items.action: A · From batch to jar · BLOCKED
items.why: Show the current manufacturing, pH control, temperature monitoring, batch identification, and release process. This cannot be scripted from public information. It becomes viable only after operations and counsel provide current documents and approve exact language.

items.action: B · One spoon, one fruit-forward ritual
items.why: Demonstrate texture, serving behavior, refrigeration, and a single flavor in an ordinary routine. Keep the promise at product use and sensory experience. Do not stack immune, energy, gut, skin, hair, and metabolism claims into the same ad.

blocks.label: Concept A · trust proof · blocked
blocks.text:
A1  Before another benefit claim, show the current batch.

A2  What changed after January 2026? Start there.

A3  Wildcrafted is the story. Current production controls are the proof.

blocks.label: Concept B · taste and ritual
blocks.text:
B1  Sea moss is easier to understand when you can see the spoonful.

B2  Real fruit, sea moss, and one repeatable place in the fridge.

B3  Start with what is in the jar, then show how it fits the routine.

sections.heading: visible *unknowns*
sections.body:
NO-LAUNCH HOLD: current manufacturing authorization, pH controls, temperature-monitoring procedures, batch traceability, testing records, recall-cohort exclusion, retailer status, approved response language, and claim substantiation are not visible in the reviewed public sources.

No safety, purity, detox, disease, immune, microbiome, metabolic, or body-outcome claim should be drafted from this public research. A founder conversation should begin with whether current-batch proof exists and can be shown.

ledger.used_for: Recall scope, reason, current terminated status
Current public positioning and benefit breadth
Post-recall retail trigger and public trust language
